exec_summary: Site traffic (GA4, 2026-05-09 to 2026-05-15): growthbook.io had 12,030 sessions and 7,769 users (-5.5% week over week).

**Site performance**
- **Overall (GA4, all traffic):** 12,030 sessions (-5.5% WoW) | 7,769 users
- **Overall (GSC, organic search):** 3,530 clicks (+2.9% WoW) | 153,105 impressions (-8.2% WoW)
- **Homepage (/):** 8,605 GA4 sessions (-10.0% WoW) all-traffic | 1,999 GSC clicks (+3.1% WoW) organic | 27,256 GSC impressions (+5.9% WoW)
- **Pricing (/pricing):** 1,235 GA4 sessions (-0.5% WoW) all-traffic | 80 GSC clicks (-13.0% WoW) organic | 6,355 GSC impressions (-6.1% WoW)
- **Docs (docs.growthbook.io):** 4,478 GA4 sessions (-7.7% WoW) all-traffic | 1,263 GSC clicks (+7.4% WoW) organic | 126,449 GSC impressions (-6.3% WoW)
- **All other pages:** 4,786 GA4 sessions (-0.9% WoW) all-traffic | 214 GSC clicks (+16.3% WoW) organic | 99,181 GSC impressions (-18.3% WoW)
Note: site performance numbers are identical to last week's payload — this appears to be the same GSC/GA4 snapshot. Flagged below under Data quality.

**New competitor activity**
- **Optimizely** continues its vertical use-case content cluster — 13 more posts detected this week (financial services homepage/mobile/offer, healthcare homepage, retail category/checkout/homepage/product/search/subscription, B2B SaaS homepage/landing/login). This campaign is now confirmed across three consecutive monitoring runs. Optimizely is methodically building page-level specificity (e.g., "checkout page," "login page") that will rank for long-tail queries GrowthBook cannot intercept without equivalent content. The window to counter-program is closing.
- **LaunchDarkly** published changelog entries for Databricks and Redshift native experimentation integrations (also detected last week, now confirmed re-appearing in this run). Additionally, a React SDK 4.0.0 changelog and a multi-SDK update signal active platform investment. Warehouse-native experimentation is now an explicit LD messaging pillar.
- **Harness** published four assets this week: A/B testing at scale for platform teams, "Experimentation Your Secret Weapon," a feature flag + pipelines resource, and an AI code sprawl / feature flag policies piece. Harness is broadening from CI/CD positioning into direct experimentation and feature flag messaging — overlap with GrowthBook's core ICP is increasing.
- **PostHog** published two community Q&A pages around experiment exposure bugs ("0 exposures" in running and completed experiments) — same switcher-capture opportunity flagged last two weeks, still not intercepted by GrowthBook content.

**New GrowthBook content**
- All 10 pages below were noticed via sitemap diff (detected 2026-05-16, real publish dates unknown). None have GSC data yet — too early to measure traction.
  - **/blog/chasing-velocity-in-a-b-testing-why-more-experiments-can-mean-less-learning** — differentiated thought-leadership angle
  - **/blog/experimentation-program-mistakes-to-avoid** — high-intent topic, competes directly with Harness/Optimizely content
  - **/blog/how-fanatics-made-experimentation-a-strategic-growth-driver** — customer story, good for bottom-funnel trust
  - **/insights/best-ab-testing-tools-developers** — targets high-value developer audience
  - **/guides/7-steps-to-better-experiment-design**, **/guides/the-a-b-testing-playbook-for-al-powered-apps**, **/blog/12-common-feature-flag-mistakes-to-avoid**, **/blog/a-practitioners-guide-to-treatment-effects-...**, **/blog/new-feature-save-time-with-automatic-metric-generation**, **/blog/growthbook-version-2-4**

**Organic movers worth watching**
- **"launchdarkly business model b2b"** holding at position 10.03 with 1,981 impressions — impressions nearly doubled from two weeks ago (851) and held last week. **/compare/growthbook-vs-launchdarkly** at position 8.3 got only 3 clicks this week. Still the highest-impression striking-distance query and still not converting.
- **"experimentation platform"** slipped to position 15.11 (was 13.1 two weeks ago, 15.1 last week) — moving in the wrong direction. At 431 impressions it remains worth defending.
- **"ab testing platform"** at position 13.24 with 357 impressions — stable but still off page 1.
- **"a/b testing software"** at position 14.55 with 321 impressions — new to striking distance this week, not in prior summaries.
- **/compare/growthbook-vs-posthog** dropped from 2 clicks to 0 this week and sits at position 4.8 with only 550 impressions over 28 days — the page ranks well but impression volume is low, suggesting thin content or narrow keyword targeting.
- **/products/experiments** still at 0 clicks (was flagged last week as a potential indexation issue — no resolution noted yet).

**Recommended actions**
- **Publish at least one vertical use-case page this week (fintech or healthcare):** Optimizely's campaign has now appeared in three consecutive monitoring runs with 13+ posts each time. Every week without a GrowthBook equivalent is a week Optimizely ages into authority on these queries.
- **Create a "warehouse-native experimentation" blog or comparison page targeting Databricks/Redshift:** LaunchDarkly's changelog entries are indexed and aging. A post targeting "Databricks A/B testing" or "Redshift experimentation" captures searches before LD builds authority. This action was recommended two weeks ago and is still outstanding.
- **Investigate /products/experiments indexation — second week at 0 clicks:** Was at 13 clicks two weeks ago. Confirm the page is crawlable and not accidentally noindexed.
- **Refresh /compare/growthbook-vs-launchdarkly title/H1 for "launchdarkly business model b2b":** 1,981 impressions at position 10.03 for the third consecutive week with minimal click conversion. A title targeting that query head-on is a low-effort move with meaningful upside.

**Data quality flags**
- GSC page-split dates show period 2026-05-04 to 2026-05-10, and GA4 week shows 2026-05-09 to 2026-05-15 — both appear to be the same snapshot as last week's summary. Site performance numbers are identical. Treat this week's site metrics as a repeat, not new data, until confirmed otherwise.
content_recommendations: 1. Write a GrowthBook vertical use-case page for fintech/financial services A/B testing this week. Optimizely has published at least 3 financial-services-specific experimentation posts across two monitoring cycles — these will rank for queries like "A/B testing for fintech" before GrowthBook has any content in that space. Prioritize homepage, mobile, and offer-page angles to mirror Optimizely's exact URL structure and intercept the same queries.

2. Write a blog post targeting "Databricks A/B testing" or "warehouse-native experimentation with Redshift." LaunchDarkly published native Databricks and Redshift experimentation changelog entries two weeks ago — those pages are now indexed and aging into authority. GrowthBook's warehouse-native story has no visible content asset capturing these searches. Recommended two weeks ago, still outstanding.

3. Optimize /compare/growthbook-vs-launchdarkly title and H1 for the query "launchdarkly business model b2b" (position 10.03, 1,981 impressions, third consecutive week in striking distance). The page is one position off page 1 and generating significant impressions with very few clicks. A targeted title refresh is the fastest path to page-1 placement on the highest-impression striking-distance query in this dataset.

4. Expand /compare/growthbook-vs-posthog with content targeting "PostHog experiment 0 exposures" and related setup troubleshooting queries. PostHog published two community Q&A pages on this exact issue. The compare page ranks at position 4.8 but generates only 550 impressions over 28 days — broadening its keyword surface with troubleshooting content would pull in frustrated PostHog users at a high-intent switcher moment.

5. Refresh /compare/growthbook-vs-statsig title and meta. Position 7.1 with 3,864 impressions over 28 days but only 1 click this week (down from 5). The impression volume is there — a more direct title ("Statsig vs GrowthBook: Side-by-Side Comparison") could recover click-through quickly.
